IDQ20845
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Initial Minor Flood Warning for the Warrego River (QLD)

Issued at 8:47 am AEST on Wednesday 21 October 2026
Flood Warning Number: 1


MINOR FLOODING POSSIBLE AT BAKERS BEND FROM SATURDAY

Isolated heavy rainfall has been recorded across the Warrego catchment for the last few
days. River levels are rising along upper parts of the catchment including moderate
flooding on the Langlo River, and minor flooding on the Nive River, and the Warrego River
upstream of Charleville.

Further moderate to heavy rain is possible with thunderstorms in the next few days which
may cause renewed river level rises or prolong the flooding.

Warrego River to Charleville:
Flooding is occurring along the Nive River and Warrego River to Charleville, with minor
flooding occurring at Biddenham and The 27 Mile Garden.

The Warrego River at Charleville is currently at 1.73 m and rising, below the minor flood
level. The Warrego River at Charleville may peak near 3.70 m overnight Thursday into
Friday, just below the minor flood level (4.0 metres).

Langlo and Ward Rivers:
Flooding is occurring along the Langlo and Ward Rivers with moderate flooding occurring at
Warilda, and minor flooding occurring at Binowee.

Warrego River downstream of Charleville:
Minor flooding is possible along the Warrego River downstream of Charleville from
Saturday.

The Warrego River at Bakers Bend is currently at 2.31 m and rising, below the minor flood
level. The Warrego River at Bakers Bend may exceed the minor flood level (5.00 m) during
Saturday 24 October with forecast rain.

Safety Advice:
* Don't drive, walk, swim or play in floodwater because it is dangerous.
* Stay away from flooded drains, rivers, streams and waterways.
* Obey road closure signs. Plan ahead so you don't drive on flooded roads.
* Check the ABC and local media for updates. The situation can change quickly, so stay
informed.
* For local emergency management warnings and advice visit
www.disaster.qld.gov.au/warnings.

For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening
emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.

Next issue:
The next warning will be issued by 11:00 AM AEST on Thursday 22 October 2026.
